limitations: Qualification covers the original complete direct-package persistence benchmark at three scales, five new complete processes per scale, on this Linux machine only.

The benchmark imports the exact native candidate index/semantic compilation and unchanged private parser/projectFacts/CallableFactCache/testkit; it does not execute the Language Server bundle or an editor during measurement.
Complete original LSP and Linux C1/C2/C3 were independently qualified on the same unchanged source/runtime before these measurements; their timings/RSS are not inferred from this benchmark.

Whole-process maxRSS includes fixture creation, cold/warm/layer-corrupt/callable-corrupt loads, cache mutation and original recursive final cleanup; per-phase interval samples are reported separately.
Testkit nearest-rank P95 over five observations equals maximum; every round and all nine phase statistics remain available.
Fresh deterministic fixture directories do not constitute a flushed operating-system disk-cache benchmark.
Warm restore is measured but has no separate original hard budget; historical normal 10k approximately 6.20-second single sample is unpaired and not a statistical comparison.
Ordinary editing, first usable protocol result, actual server/workers memory, full platform/mode/tool matrix and long sessions still require evidence.
Normal product remains unchanged; original 157.74/150 ms Controller and 920.54/768 MiB normal 10k failures remain open.
No adoption, installation or publication; complete C1-C4/R4, P0-P9/F01-F14 and human WSL objective remains active.
nextStep: Inspect warm-restore waiting cost and validate ordinary editing plus actual server/worker performance on the unchanged candidate before deciding product adoption; preserve the original budgets and full acceptance scope.
